articles.title: Olivine won the game. The next week got harder.
articles.dek: A shutout moved the Ironclads above .500. Injuries to Veluza, Kabutops and Thievul made the celebration considerably more complicated.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: A 14–0 score is usually an invitation to write a reassuring sentence. The defense allowed nothing. The offense supplied enough. The team goes home with a victory and a better record. Olivine earned all of that at Snowpoint. The Ironclads also left the week with three new absences that make reassurance feel a little careless.

Veluza is listed out five weeks. Kabutops has four remaining. Thievul has six. These are different players with different jobs, and the losses should not be compressed into the phrase “a few injuries” simply because the score looks pleasant. The Ironclads are 5–4 and currently sixth in the Kanto–Johto playoff order. They have reached a useful position just as keeping it becomes more complicated.

I don't think the correct response is to decide that the win was somehow unfortunate. A team cannot trade its result back for healthier circumstances. Olivine needed this victory, earned it and gets to keep it. My concern is with the familiar habit of turning everybody who remains available into a cheerful promise that nothing will change. Something has changed. Jasmine's next job is to make the change manageable, not invisible.
The win matters. So do the players we won't have. We can be proud of the first without pretending the second is easy. Everyone deserves to know what we're asking of them next.
body.speaker: Jasmine

body.text: That strikes me as a more useful beginning than a speech about adversity. A speech can be delivered without resolving a single assignment. Naming the work takes longer. It also has the advantage of helping the person who actually has to do it.
A receiver's absence has a shape

Veluza caught six passes for fifty yards against Snowpoint. That was thirty percent of Drampa's twenty completions. Across the season, the tight end has 36 catches for 386 yards. This is a receiving contribution that has accumulated over nine games, not a player who became important only when the injury list made us notice. Removing him changes where the quarterback has repeatedly found useful work.

Drampa was twenty-of-twenty-five for 179 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in the shutout. It was the sort of afternoon that can appear modest beside somebody else's larger yardage total and still be exactly what a team requires. Eighty percent of his throws were completed. Olivine scored twice through the air and did not give Snowpoint an interception. The quarterback has earned credit for that without being asked to promise an identical result with a different group around him.
I'll take responsibility for getting us organized. We know what Veluza gives us. The next people deserve throws they can make something of, not a lecture about the player who's missing.
body.speaker: Drampa

body.text: I like that answer because it contains a job rather than a slogan. The quarterback cannot replace a teammate by admiring him more intensely. He can help the available receivers understand what a successful possession will ask of them. Delcatty caught two passes for 34 yards at Snowpoint. Magmar had four for forty. Gastrodon added three for 29. Those contributions belong to the win, though none is a guarantee about next week's distribution.
Veluza's response was characteristically direct.
I want to be out there. Until I can be, I can still be useful to the people taking the work. They don't need me telling them how hard my week is.
body.speaker: Veluza

body.text: There is generosity in that, but I would not turn it into an obligation to sound brave every day. An injured player is allowed to miss playing. The team is allowed to miss him. Football coverage sometimes becomes so determined to find an inspiring angle that it forgets the basic disappointment sitting in front of it.
Two losses on the other side of the ball

Kabutops is an outside linebacker. Thievul is a cornerback. Their absences reach into different parts of the defense that just held Snowpoint scoreless. Olivine limited the Blizzard to forty-six rushing yards and received a sack from Beedrill. It was a complete result worth recognizing. It was also achieved in a game after which the available personnel became less complete.

There are no firm return dates to circle yet. What Jasmine knows now is enough to make planning difficult: a receiving contributor, a linebacker and a corner are unavailable for multiple weeks. Stantler's existing season-ending absence remains on the list as well. The roster was already carrying an absence before these arrived. Gastrodon also picked up a minor injury at Snowpoint, though he has no remaining absence listed.
The people stepping in have helped us all season. I want them to feel supported. Nobody needs to carry my frustration along with their own assignment.
body.speaker: Kabutops

body.text: There is a quiet difference between that and claiming every replacement will be seamless. Kabutops is offering support, not a forecast. The distinction matters. Teammates can make an uncomfortable transition less lonely without pretending that experience, timing and familiarity transfer automatically with a position on a depth chart.

Olivine's season has already contained two shutout losses, 21–0 at Lavender and 19–0 at Eterna. It has also contained an overtime win over Mahogany and a three-point victory against Dewford. The record has moved through enough different kinds of afternoons to discourage a tidy identity. Now the Ironclads have won twice in succession, beating Oreburgh 29–10 before the Snowpoint shutout. Forty-three points scored and ten allowed over two games is real progress in the results. It does not settle what happens with the next lineup.

The latest win wasn't effortless. Olivine lost a Gabite fumble after moving 68 yards on its second possession. The defense forced a punt, and the next offensive drive covered 67 yards for the first touchdown. The second scoring drive took thirteen plays and crossed from the third quarter into the fourth, ending with Drampa's one-yard short-left throw to Quilladin. There was recovery from a mistake and patience through a long possession. Those are habits worth trying to carry forward, even when the people doing the work change.
Keep the win, adjust the expectations

Canalave visits next. The Bulwark arrives at 6–4 after a 34–0 loss, and the matchup offers each offense an immediate reason to take its preparation seriously. Olivine's margin over .500 is one game. Its place in the current playoff order is useful, temporary and subject to other people playing football. This would be an inconvenient time to confuse a position in the current table with something already secured.

My expectation is not that Jasmine will make the injuries irrelevant. That is a demand designed to disappoint everyone. I want to see an offense that gives its available receivers clear work and a defense that knows where the new responsibilities begin. If a drive looks different because Veluza isn't there, that can be an adjustment rather than evidence of panic. If the defense needs time to settle, the offense can help it by remaining functional.

The Ironclads earned the right to enjoy a shutout. They also earned a difficult week of practical questions. Both can be true without reducing the victory to a footnote or using it to cover up the cost. I would keep the celebration brief enough that everyone gets included, then turn toward the people whose next assignment just grew. Five wins are already on the record. The work of finding the sixth has become more personal.

articles.title: Byron, the defense cannot play quarterback.
articles.dek: Canalave still owns six wins. Its offense has reached fourteen points only twice in ten games, and Dorian Pike is done calling that a charming preference.
articles.author: dorian-pike

body.text: Let us begin respectfully. Canalave has six wins. Byron has put a team into the current playoff field. The Bulwark has held opponents to 137 points across ten games, and a defense allowing 13.7 per game is doing enough useful work to deserve more than a shrug. There. Respect delivered. Please keep the receipt, because the rest of this conversation is going to cost something.

Canalave scored zero against Mt. Silver. The final was 34–0. Slowking completed eight of fifteen passes for 63 yards, no touchdowns and an interception. The running game supplied ninety-one yards, eighty-six of them from Gabite, and the scoreboard never moved. If your explanation begins and ends with the quality of the opponent, I invite you to examine the preceding nine games before handing in the assignment.

And here's the uncomfortable truth: this offense was a problem while Canalave was winning, and six victories have been used as a very attractive curtain. The Bulwark has scored 116 points in ten games. Eleven point six per game. It has reached fourteen points twice. Twice! The other eight afternoons have asked the defense to protect thirteen points or fewer, sometimes considerably fewer, and twice absolutely none.
That is not a sustainable expression of toughness. That is an unpaid invoice addressed to the defense.
Gabite found yards. Canalave lost possessions.

Gabite carried sixteen times for eighty-six yards against the Reds. More than five yards per carry. Canalave was not deprived of every useful offensive action. It had a runner producing yardage, and it still finished without a point. This is why I become impatient when the explanation for a shutout is reduced to a demand for greater commitment. Commitment to what, specifically? The runner was already gaining ground. He also lost a fumble on a ten-yard run up the middle early in the third quarter. The useful yards and the damaging mistake belong in the same sentence.

I can count the yards. I can count the points too. And yes, I can remember the fumble without being reminded. Apparently we're all very impressed with one number until it's time to discuss the others.
body.speaker: Gabite

body.text: Correct, Gabite. The yardage deserves acknowledgment. It also deserves company. Slowking's 63 passing yards came on eight completions. Granbull caught two passes for nineteen yards. Those are recorded contributions, not an accusation that the people involved failed to care. But we are discussing an offense responsible for finishing possessions, and the overall production did not come close to completing that responsibility.

The turnovers make the failure sharper. Canalave lost the ball on a punt return before its offense had run a play. Slowking then threw an interception early in the second quarter and lost a fumble late in the half. Gabite's fumble made four giveaways in total. Mt. Silver scored on the possession immediately following each: touchdown, field goal, field goal, touchdown. Twenty points. The offense was not merely failing to help; together with the return unit, it was providing the opponent additional opportunities.

For the season, Slowking has 1,008 passing yards, six touchdown passes and three interceptions. Ten games. Six touchdown passes. He has also been sacked nineteen times. The interception total is low enough to support a claim of restraint. It cannot carry an entire argument for the offense. Avoiding mistakes has value; creating so little that the opponent can survive your mistake-free stretches has consequences too.

I am not asking Byron to wake up tomorrow and announce forty passes because Dorian Pike raised his voice. I raise it regularly. That would be a dreadful basis for personnel planning. I am asking for an offense with an answer when the first useful run is followed by a situation that requires a throw. The passing game must threaten something beyond the possibility that the punt unit might get a slightly better starting point.
I'm aware the defense would prefer a little company on the scoreboard. So would I. We can either keep admiring how careful we've been or give ourselves something worth protecting.
body.speaker: Slowking

body.text: There is a quarterback who has identified the meeting's agenda. Good. Now make the agenda visible on the field.
The defense is allowed to have a bad afternoon

Delcatty, number 57, recorded three sacks against Mt. Silver. Three. Canalave's defense did not spend the entire game watching politely from a distance. It generated disruption, and the opponent still scored thirty-four. That can happen against a very good team. What cannot continue is the assumption that every defensive effort must also manufacture the conditions for an offense that has no independent scoring floor.

The Bulwark has twenty sacks this season. Passimian has eight; Delcatty now has four. It has allowed 575 rushing yards over ten games. These are useful achievements. I will not pretend that thirty-four points allowed was a good defensive result merely because I have chosen to interrogate the offense. I will insist that the defense's wider body of work is precisely why the lack of offensive help has become so exhausting to watch.

Canalave beat Eterna 10–6. It beat Oreburgh 13–6, Celadon 9–7 and Azalea 13–0. Every one counts. Nobody is proposing to deduct victories because they offended the entertainment committee. But the pattern tells us what the team keeps requiring: hold somebody almost silent, then hope the offense produces just enough sound to be heard over them.

When that requirement fails, the margin becomes enormous. Snowpoint won 35–0 in Week 2. Mt. Silver has now won 34–0. Those opponents do not have the same record, which should complicate any attempt to explain both results as unavoidable encounters with the league's elite. The common feature is Canalave's zero. The offense supplied no means of resistance on the scoreboard either time.

We have won games with defense, but that doesn't excuse what we haven't produced. We need to give the offense workable answers and expect it to finish. The record doesn't make that responsibility smaller.
body.speaker: Byron

body.text: No, Byron. It makes the opportunity larger. You are 6–4. You are still positioned to make something of the season. This is exactly when a coach should demand a correction, before a problem becomes a retrospective explanation for why a promising year got away.
Do not wait for another shutout to ask

The last five games have produced thirteen, nine, thirteen, thirteen and zero points. Forty-eight in total. Canalave went 3–2 in that stretch because the defense kept handing the offense chances to survive. I am not confusing a winning stretch with a failure. I am identifying the part that makes the next winning stretch so difficult to reproduce.

Olivine is next. The Ironclads just won 14–0, moved to 5–4 and picked up multiple injuries. That is an opponent with its own problems, not permission to assume the Bulwark can win another game by waiting. Canalave needs to arrive with a passing game that contributes meaningfully, a runner whose work becomes part of finished possessions and protection that gives those ideas time to exist.

I have heard enough praise for the romance of low-scoring football. Low scoring can be tense, disciplined and excellent. It can also be an offense borrowing its reputation from the people who keep rescuing it. Byron has a useful defense and a live season. Slowking has an opportunity to turn six touchdown passes into the beginning of a better story. Gabite has demonstrated that a productive run is still available.

Now put them together. Ask for more than survival. Ask the offense to create something the defense can protect. Six wins are a reason to act with urgency, not a reason to pretend the problem has already been solved.

articles.title: Week 11: Sunyshore and Blackthorn get the argument to themselves
articles.dek: A one-point call between contenders, Eterna’s test at unbeaten Mt. Silver, and every other matchup. Tessa Wren sets 28 checkable keys before the five-writer panel makes its 70 picks.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: My Week 10 card finished 10–4 with three shared closest-score bonuses. Rustboro, Sootopolis, Cianwood and Pastoria supplied the four corrections. Rowan and Mara each went 9–5; Ellis went 8–6 and collected six closest-score bonuses. Dorian finished 6–8. These records grade saved predictions, not the more attractive forecasts any of us may now remember making.

The keys deserve their own audit. Mossdeep won despite missing my 140-yard rushing target with ninety-six and allowing four sacks instead of no more than two. Cinnabar met both of my published keys—Rustboro stayed below 150 rushing yards and Gholdengo threw no interception—yet lost because the Stone threw five touchdown passes. Mt. Silver did meet its turnover and return-defense targets. A correct winner can hide a poor explanation; an apparently successful key can overlook the way a game actually changes.

Week 11 has fourteen games. Viridian, Cinnabar, Rustboro and Mauville are off. Sunyshore at Blackthorn leads my slate, with Eterna at Mt. Silver close behind. Mossdeep visits Vermilion after its late escape against Saffron, while Saffron tests Fortree’s three-game recovery. Every matchup below gets a score and one measurable key for each side. The season panel totals count only picks saved before the games, beginning in Week 5; closest-score bonuses remain separate from winner records.

matchups.matchup: Petalburg’s modest offense meets Pewter’s stubborn defense
matchups.analysis: Petalburg is 6–3 after a 14–7 win in which Oinkologne ran for seventy-five yards and Iron Valiant threw two touchdowns. Pewter returns from its bye at 4–5 with only seventy-seven points scored, but a defense that has allowed 120. I favor the Pride because their latest game offered enough rushing support to survive a limited passing total. The Rockers can keep this close if their defense makes Petalburg's protection problems recur: Viridian collected three sacks. Brock's cornerback absences make long defensive possessions uncomfortable, so the home offense needs more than occasional movement. This is a game where an extra successful third down could matter more than an impressive yardage total.
matchups.awayKey: Rush for at least ninety yards and allow no more than two sacks.
matchups.homeKey: Force two turnovers and score at least two touchdowns.

matchups.matchup: Dewford returns rested; Celadon needs a broader offensive answer
matchups.analysis: The Breakers are 5–4 after their bye, with Ambipom's 175 scrimmage yards against Viridian still the clearest picture of their threat. Celadon is 2–8 after losing 24–6 at Mauville. Seaking ran for seventy-six yards, but the Bloom managed ninety-nine passing yards. I expect Dewford to offer too many productive ways through the defense for Celadon to cover with a one-dimensional response. The danger is familiar: the Breakers' two turnovers in their last game made an overtime escape necessary. Erika's team can keep the result available if it wins those extra possessions. Dewford should have the better attack; it still needs to prevent its own mistakes from making that distinction irrelevant.
matchups.awayKey: Gain at least 300 total yards and commit no more than one turnover.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Dewford below 120 rushing yards and finish three scoring drives.

matchups.matchup: Cerulean gets another chance to turn passing yards into points
matchups.analysis: The Tide are 4–5 after a second consecutive loss. Farigiraf threw for 251 yards at Fortree, yet Cerulean scored nine and ran for twenty-five. Lavaridge is 3–6 after a 21–7 win, its defense finally making a useful offensive afternoon count. I take Cerulean narrowly at home because the passing game still creates opportunities and the Inferno's season-long defensive record remains difficult. That is not permission to repeat forty-five throws for one touchdown. Flannery's team can win if last week's resistance survives against a better passing total and Delphox supplies another careful two-touchdown game. I am asking the Tide to improve their finishing, not awarding them credit for doing it in advance.
matchups.awayKey: Keep Cerulean below 250 passing yards and lose no turnovers.
matchups.homeKey: Rush for at least seventy yards and convert three red-zone trips into touchdowns.

matchups.matchup: Fortree’s streak reaches its hardest defensive examination
matchups.analysis: Fortree has won three straight to reach 3–6, with Floatzel's eighty-four rushing yards and Dunsparce's eight catches helping beat Cerulean. Saffron is 7–2 after a 20–17 loss at Mossdeep, where its depleted rush still collected four sacks. I expect the Psi Corps to make Fortree's recent offense work much harder for sustained possessions. Brooks and Ninetales remain out two weeks, so the available rushers must repeat useful work rather than await reinforcements. For the Skyhawks, Rabsca avoiding sacks and turnovers matters more than producing one spectacular completion. Saffron's offense had 334 yards against Mossdeep; cleaner possession management should be enough to turn that kind of movement into a home recovery.
matchups.awayKey: Allow no more than two sacks and produce three scoring drives.
matchups.homeKey: Win the turnover margin and hold Fortree below 100 rushing yards.

matchups.matchup: An unbeaten visitor meets an increasingly expensive secondary problem
matchups.analysis: Mossdeep is 9–0 after recovering from 17–6 down to beat Saffron 20–17. Accel BeckhmJr caught both touchdown passes, while the defense kept the second half scoreless. Marshall Flock is now out five weeks, an important change for the next stretch. Vermilion is 6–3 after allowing Drampa three touchdown passes in a 24–10 loss to Sootopolis, with both Tentacruel and Delcatty still absent at cornerback. I expect Dram Marino and the Eclipse receivers to create enough favorable passing possessions to overcome their own defensive disruption. Chandelure can make the game uncomfortable if he exploits that disruption and gets more support than last week's sixty rushing yards. The Volts need pressure; zero sacks against Sootopolis is an ominous starting point.
matchups.awayKey: Complete at least twenty passes and allow no more than two sacks.
matchups.homeKey: Force two turnovers and score at least two passing touchdowns.

matchups.matchup: Can Sootopolis make one clean passing afternoon repeatable?
matchups.analysis: Sootopolis is 4–5 after its most persuasive recent response: Drampa went twenty-for-twenty-six for 233 yards and three touchdowns against Vermilion, without a sack or interception. Fuchsia fell to 1–9 after scoring seven at Lavaridge. Empoleon still generated 212 passing yards, but no touchdown pass. I favor the Surge because their latest protection and finishing offered a more complete route to points. The Shadows have enough passing production to challenge an opponent that has conceded 204 this season. They must convert it into more than a long statistical conversation. Wallace's team should expect resistance; what it needs to show now is that last week's efficient offense can survive a road game against a different defense.
matchups.awayKey: Throw at least two touchdown passes and commit no more than one turnover.
matchups.homeKey: Score touchdowns on three possessions and sack Drampa at least twice.

matchups.matchup: Two offenses with useful pieces and very little recent reward
matchups.analysis: Azalea is 4–6 after losing 27–13 at Eterna, where the Swarm ran for twenty-five yards and allowed four sacks. Oreburgh is 2–8 after a 28–17 loss despite 137 receiving yards from Furret and seventy-seven rushing from Diggersby. Cryogonal's two interceptions helped make those gains insufficient. I give Azalea a narrow home edge because the Miners keep making productive offense pay an additional turnover tax. The Swarm cannot rely on that forecast to repair their own protection. Oreburgh can win by keeping the ball and forcing Bugsy's attack to build long scoring drives; Azalea can answer by getting a much more useful early-down run game than Eterna permitted.
matchups.awayKey: Throw no interceptions and gain at least 100 rushing yards.
matchups.homeKey: Allow no more than two sacks and finish three touchdown drives.

matchups.matchup: Eterna’s improving attack visits the other unbeaten team
matchups.analysis: Mt. Silver is 9–0 after beating Canalave 34–0. Tic Thorpe threw three touchdowns and ran for a fourth, while the Reds took the ball away four times and gave it away none. Eterna is 6–3 with a defense allowing 77 points through nine games. Stantler's 140 rushing yards against Azalea gave that defense substantial help. This is the matchup I most want to see after Sunyshore–Blackthorn: a serious defensive opponent forcing Connor McLarren's team to earn its scoring opportunities. I favor Mt. Silver because its latest offense combined productive passing with clean possession management, although Gregar Jenings is now out two weeks at receiver and that production must be redistributed. The Thorns' route is to make that passing less comfortable and preserve Stantler's influence without letting a deficit remove the run from the afternoon. A four-turnover gift package should not be assumed to arrive twice.
matchups.awayKey: Rush for at least 120 yards and commit no more than one turnover.
matchups.homeKey: Convert at least six third downs and hold Eterna below twenty points.

matchups.matchup: Canalave needs points before it needs a statement
matchups.analysis: Olivine is 5–4 after a 14–0 win at Snowpoint, its second consecutive victory. Canalave is 6–4 after a 34–0 loss in which Slowking threw for sixty-three yards and the team lost four turnovers. I expect the Ironclads to make the Bulwark construct more offense than that recent performance suggests they can reliably produce. Delcatty's three sacks against Mt. Silver show that Canalave can still disrupt a passer; the problem is rewarding those stops. Olivine has fresh absences for Veluza at tight end (five weeks), Kabutops at outside linebacker (four) and Thievul at cornerback (six), so another fourteen-point game is possible rather than comfortable. Drampa's twenty completions in twenty-five attempts last week give the home side a practical route to the extra scoring possession.
matchups.awayKey: Commit no more than one turnover and score on three possessions.
matchups.homeKey: Complete at least eighteen passes and hold Canalave below 200 total yards.

matchups.matchup: A small passing total finally meant something for Cianwood
matchups.analysis: Victreebel threw four touchdowns on seventy-eight passing yards as Cianwood beat Oreburgh 28–17. That is efficient finishing, not a promise that the same ratio will recur. Swampert's ninety-two rushing yards provide the more useful foundation for the next assignment. Snowpoint is 2–7 after a 14–0 loss, with only forty-six rushing yards. I favor the 3–7 Crushers at home because their available offense has finally shown a way to turn modest movement into points. Candice's team can reverse that expectation by forcing longer fields and giving its own passing game a more balanced workload. Neither side has earned a forecast of comfortable scoring, but Cianwood at least enters with evidence of finishing possessions.
matchups.awayKey: Gain at least eighty rushing yards and score touchdowns on two possessions.
matchups.homeKey: Rush for at least 100 yards and allow no more than one passing touchdown.

matchups.matchup: Violet’s defensive streak meets Hearthome’s increasingly useful offense
matchups.analysis: The Falcons are 5–4 after three straight wins, the latest 14–6 at Veilstone. Hearthome is 3–6–1 after losing 27–25 to Blackthorn, with Frosmoth throwing two touchdowns. I favor Violet narrowly because it has repeatedly made opponents struggle to finish, while the Haunts still carry significant absences including Luxray and Sunflora. That call needs humility: Hearthome has just scored twenty-five against one of the league's strongest teams, and Violet's own offense has not offered much cushion. Iron Jugulis must use the receiving chances without the interception that appeared last week. Fantina's team can win if its recent passing production persists and the defense makes the Falcons play from behind.
matchups.awayKey: Throw at least two touchdown passes and allow fewer than 100 rushing yards.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Hearthome below twenty points and lose no turnovers.

matchups.matchup: Lavender and Veilstone both need the offense to join the game
matchups.analysis: Lavender is 4–5 after losing 17–7 at Pastoria. Mr. Clanky completed nine of twenty-six for ninety-six yards, and the only Wails touchdown came on a punt return. Veilstone is 4–6 after scoring six against Violet, with Tatsugiri throwing two interceptions and no touchdowns. I take Lavender narrowly at home because the receiving group has shown a higher productive ceiling earlier in the season. That is a recovery forecast, not a description of last week. The Fists have enough defensive resistance to make another poor Wails passing day decisive. Travis Scarboro needs sustained offensive possessions; Maylene needs the ball to stop returning to the opponent before those possessions can finish.
matchups.awayKey: Commit no turnovers and score at least two offensive touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Complete at least eighteen passes and convert four third downs.

matchups.matchup: Pastoria’s passing revival travels to a rested, awkward opponent
matchups.analysis: Mahogany returns from its bye at 3–5–1 and plus-fourteen. Pastoria is 3–6 after beating Lavender 17–7 behind 230 passing yards from Togekiss and eighty-nine receiving from Farigiraf. I favor the Frost at home because their season-long scoring balance has been stronger, even though their record has repeatedly failed to reward competitive afternoons. Kricketune remains out ten weeks, leaving a defensive responsibility that the Waves can test. Pastoria's forty-two rushing yards last week kept much of the burden on its passing game. Pryce's team needs to make that burden heavier without conceding the kind of long receiving touchdown that finished the Lavender win. Another tie would be an unusually literal refusal to settle the argument.
matchups.awayKey: Pass for at least 225 yards and commit no more than one turnover.
matchups.homeKey: Rush for at least 100 yards and score touchdowns on three possessions.

matchups.matchup: Sunyshore–Blackthorn: two contenders, one uncomfortable road pick
matchups.analysis: Blackthorn is 8–1 after escaping Hearthome 27–25. Hatterene completed seventeen of twenty-one for 249 yards and two touchdowns, but the Dragons ran for forty-nine yards and now have Grovyle out six weeks. Sunyshore arrives from its bye at 7–2, with Myles Gabite still absent three weeks. My narrow pick is the Starseekers. Their latest game combined 160 rushing yards with a twenty-point second half at Lavender, and I expect that balance to give the rested visitors enough possession to challenge Blackthorn's efficient passing. The choice is close because Hatterene has repeatedly made a modest number of attempts productive. Karson Jones needs pressure without gifting easy completions; Clair needs a better running contribution than Hearthome allowed. I would not turn either record into a reason to expect comfort. This is the week's best argument between two teams already entitled to believe they belong near the top.
matchups.awayKey: Rush for at least 120 yards and surrender no more than one turnover.
matchups.homeKey: Complete at least seventy percent of passes and hold Sunyshore below 100 rushing yards.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Pewter has allowed 120 points in nine games; Petalburg just won with fourteen. I expect the rested Rockers to turn that modest scoring appetite into a home upset, helped by the protection problems that produced three Pride sacks allowed.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Oinkologne's seventy-five rushing yards gave Norman a workable foundation against Viridian. I expect that foundation to keep Petalburg out of the obvious passing situations Pewter needs, while the Rockers' limited offense struggles to supply an answer.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Rockers have stayed involved in the season without asking their offense for much. I think the bye helps them find one extra useful possession against a Pride team that still has little margin when the passing game is quiet.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Seventy-seven points. In nine games. Petalburg does not need to stage an offensive revolution to beat that. I expect Norman's runners to provide enough support that Pewter cannot hide its scoring problem behind another respectable defensive afternoon.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Petalburg's recent rushing contribution offers the steadier way to maintain possession. Pewter can pressure the passer, but I expect the Pride to avoid enough long-yardage situations to finish one more scoring drive than the home offense.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Dewford needed overtime last time because it kept offering Viridian invitations. Celadon just threw for ninety-nine yards. I expect Ambipom to make the rested Breakers' next win considerably less dependent on an apology and a late kick.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Bloom stopped Mauville's running game and still lost by eighteen. I expect Dewford's ability to involve Ambipom in multiple ways to stretch that defensive workload further, without relying on one type of gain to sustain every drive.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Celadon has had a difficult stretch of disrupted personnel and incomplete offensive afternoons. I expect the rested Breakers' established contributors to make that uncertainty matter, even if Erika's runners keep the game competitive for a while.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Dewford's last win required a field goal with eight seconds left and overtime. That is not a royal procession. I expect Celadon's running game to keep the ball away, then another Breakers mistake to become the home team's opening.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Breakers have the broader recent offensive case, while Celadon's limited passing makes sustained scoring harder. I expect Dewford to gain enough from both Ambipom's rushing and receiving work to survive a few imperfect possessions.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Cerulean turned 251 passing yards into nine points and would like us to admire the yardage. I prefer Lavaridge's newly discovered habit of scoring touchdowns while allowing only seven. The Inferno get the upset until the Tide finish something.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Lavaridge's seven points allowed were useful, but Cerulean can challenge more of the field than Fuchsia finished last week. I expect Misty's passing game to find enough receiving opportunities to win, provided it gets even modest help on the ground.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Tide's two recent losses have exposed different problems, which makes a total collapse too simple a verdict. I expect a narrow home recovery against a defense whose improved latest game has not erased the longer record.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Nine points after fifty-six allowed the previous week. Cerulean is fixing one room while the next catches fire. I expect Delphox's careful passing to carry Lavaridge's improvement forward and force Misty to explain another unused collection of yards.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Cerulean still produced 251 passing yards at Fortree, and Lavaridge's broader defensive record remains vulnerable. I expect enough of that passing movement to become touchdowns at home, although the Tide's rushing weakness keeps the margin small.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Saffron sacked Marino four times without Brooks and came within three points of ruining Mossdeep's perfect record. Fortree has won three, which is charming. I expect the Psi Corps defense to make the fourth application considerably less enjoyable.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Skyhawks have used productive rushing to support Rabsca, but Saffron just held Mossdeep to ninety-six on the ground. I expect that front to make Fortree's passing downs more difficult than the recent winning streak has required.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Fortree's recovery deserves to be treated as real progress. I still expect Saffron's established defense to make the next step too large, especially if the Psi Corps turn their own 334-yard performance into cleaner possessions this time.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Winona has won three straight. Trent Scarboro has just watched a 17–6 lead disappear. I expect Fortree to carry its balance into this game while Saffron's mistakes leave the door open for a much louder fourth victory.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Psi Corps created pressure against a stronger offense than Fortree's recent opponents. I expect that disruption to limit Rabsca's comfortable completions, with Saffron's receivers producing enough scoring to turn a close loss into a home response.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Vermilion has six wins and a negative point differential, a balancing act I would not hire for children's parties. Its depleted secondary just allowed three touchdown passes without a sack. I expect Marino to make the same weakness expensive.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Dorrill's offense survived Saffron's pressure because it still had ways to finish. Vermilion produced no sack against Sootopolis and remains depleted at corner. I expect Mossdeep's receiving matchups to create separation before the Volts can exploit Flock's absence.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Mossdeep's narrow win showed an ability to stay involved when the early game was uncomfortable. I expect that patience to travel, while Vermilion's defensive absences make it difficult to protect a lead even if Chandelure starts well.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: I remain available to criticize Michael Dorrill. I am not obliged to pretend Vermilion's injured secondary is a convincing vehicle for it. Marino should find too many favorable throws, and the Eclipse should make this less dramatic than last week.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Volts' latest defense allowed efficient passing without generating pressure. I expect Mossdeep's passing game to exploit that combination, while its own remaining defenders do enough to keep Chandelure's response from matching a fuller Eclipse attack.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Drampa completed twenty of twenty-six without a sack or interception. Fuchsia answered its own manageable opponent with seven points. I expect Sootopolis to repeat enough of the clean passing to win, even if the Surge return to making it nervous.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Sootopolis has allowed 204 points, and one tidy passing day does not repair that defense. I expect Empoleon to turn his usual yardage into a few actual finishes against this opponent, while the Shadows finally make productive throws matter.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Fuchsia's record is bleak, but its passing game has kept producing opportunities that the endings have wasted. Against a Surge defense with a difficult season behind it, I think one of those afternoons finally reaches a better conclusion.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Empoleon threw for 212 yards and no touchdowns against Lavaridge. No touchdowns. I expect Drampa's cleaner finishing to expose the difference between moving the football and putting the opponent under actual scoring pressure. Sootopolis gets the points that matter.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Sootopolis' latest protection gave Drampa time to turn completions into three touchdowns. I expect that more complete offensive sequence to continue against Fuchsia, whose passing yards have too often stopped short of a comparable scoring return.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Furret had 137 receiving yards and Diggersby ran for seventy-seven. Oreburgh's useful parts are visible, even when the result is ugly. I expect fewer gifts this time and enough offense to punish an Azalea team still struggling to protect its passer.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Miners' interceptions keep undoing good rushing and receiving work. I expect Azalea's defense to create another short-field opportunity, and the Swarm's offense to recover enough against a less restrictive opponent than Eterna to use it.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Neither recent loss invites confidence. I give Azalea the smallest home edge because Oreburgh's recurring mistakes make its productive stretches harder to trust, while the Swarm should find more room than Eterna allowed them last week.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Oreburgh just allowed four touchdown passes on seventy-eight passing yards. That is a spectacularly poor exchange rate. I expect Azalea to take the opportunities the Miners keep offering and make its own limited offense look adequate for an afternoon.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Azalea should face less sustained pressure than Eterna applied, while Oreburgh's turnover pattern creates chances to shorten the field. I expect that combination to give the Swarm one more successful possession in an otherwise close game.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Eterna has finally brought an offense to its defensive meetings. Unfortunately, Mt. Silver just scored thirty-four while allowing nothing. I expect Tic Thorpe to create enough passing production that the Thorns need more than another useful Stantler afternoon.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Stantler gives Eterna a credible way to keep the game manageable, but Mt. Silver just paired clean possession management with productive third downs. I expect that passing consistency to force the Thorns beyond the scoring pace they prefer.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Thorns' defense has earned a proper examination against an unbeaten team. I think Stantler can preserve enough possession for it to provide one, and Eterna can win a game in which the Reds receive fewer convenient turnovers.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Connor McLarren's team won 34–0. Tic Thorpe accounted for four touchdowns. Eterna is a serious opponent, and the Reds will treat it seriously by scoring enough to make another excellent defensive afternoon insufficient. Nine unbeaten becomes ten.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mt. Silver's latest offense converted seven of thirteen third downs without a turnover. I expect Eterna to reduce that efficiency but not eliminate it, while the Reds' defense makes the Thorns build more passing production than last week required.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Canalave lost four turnovers and scored zero, which is a very efficient way to look hopeless. I expect a cleaner afternoon to reveal a better team than that score, with Delcatty's pressure making Olivine's limited scoring cushion disappear.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Bulwark created three sacks and still produced only sixty-three passing yards. I expect Olivine to keep that passing game constrained, while Drampa's short, accurate work supplies enough possession to make Canalave's isolated pressures insufficient.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Olivine has answered its own shutout loss with two wins. I expect that steadier offense to hold up at home against a Canalave team still trying to reconnect defensive effort with offensive reward. The margin need not be large to be convincing.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Byron's team scored zero while Delcatty did enough rushing to collect three sacks. Reward the defense, for once. Until Canalave demonstrates that it can, I expect Olivine's recent habit of completing passes to produce the larger useful number.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Drampa's twenty-for-twenty-five performance offers Olivine a dependable way to sustain drives. Canalave's pressure should disrupt some possessions, but I expect its limited passing response to leave the home side with the extra touchdown it needs.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Four touchdowns on seventy-eight passing yards is not a ratio I would frame as a business plan. Swampert's ninety-two rushing yards are more reassuring. I expect that foundation to be enough against a Snowpoint offense fresh from zero points.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Cianwood can ask Swampert to carry more of the ordinary early-down work and keep Victreebel's passing decisions modest. I expect Snowpoint's limited rushing to make its own offense easier to contain, even without another extraordinary touchdown rate.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Crushers finally had an afternoon in which the available players could see their work become points. I expect that practical confidence, backed by Swampert's running, to survive a home game against a Blizzard team struggling to finish anything.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Seventy-eight passing yards will not normally buy four touchdowns. I expect Snowpoint to make Cianwood travel farther for its points, then discover enough offense against the Crushers to make last week's spectacular efficiency look like a temporary bargain.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Swampert provides Cianwood a more repeatable foundation than the four-touchdown passing line alone. I expect that running contribution to preserve enough scoring chances, while Snowpoint continues struggling to support its passing game with useful rushing.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Violet has won three straight by making other offenses equally uncomfortable. Hearthome just made Blackthorn sweat, but I expect the Falcons' repeated defensive resistance to matter more than another Haunts argument that the loss was almost impressive.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Hearthome produced 217 passing yards and two passing touchdowns against Blackthorn without allowing a sack. I expect that protection to make Violet work harder than its recent opponents did, with Frosmoth supplying enough scoring to overturn a small home edge.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Haunts keep showing more usable offense than their record advertises. I think that progress can survive this trip, and Violet's small scoring margins leave room for the visitor's latest passing improvement to become a win instead of another near miss.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Violet's latest opponent scored six. Hearthome's latest opponent scored twenty-seven. I expect the Falcons to keep this in their preferred neighborhood, then force Fantina's team to explain another close result without receiving another victory.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Violet has repeated its ability to limit offensive finishing, while Hearthome still carries important absences. I expect the Falcons to reduce the Haunts' recent passing efficiency enough that one extra home touchdown decides a narrow game.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Lavender completed nine passes; Veilstone threw two interceptions. Selecting a winner should come with a folding chair and a long sigh. I expect the Wails' earlier receiving production to reappear just often enough to survive at home.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Lavender's only touchdown last week came on a punt return, and its offense converted one of nine third downs. I expect Veilstone's defense to sustain that discomfort, while the Fists protect the ball just well enough to win a modest scoring exchange.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Wails' recent collapse is real, but the receiving group's better afternoons were real too. I expect a home response against another limited offense, with enough sustained possessions to let the defense protect something other than a special-teams rescue.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Nine completions. Ninety-six yards. Travis Scarboro cannot keep asking us to remember the good stretches while the present offense disappears. I expect Veilstone's pressure and a more careful Tatsugiri to turn Lavender's current problem into another loss.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Lavender has shown more offensive range earlier in the season than Veilstone's recent attack. I expect a limited recovery at home, with the Wails finding enough completions to edge an opponent that still struggles to finish possessions without turnovers.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Mahogany's positive differential has been requesting a better record for weeks. Pastoria just found a competent passing afternoon, but I expect the rested Frost to make that improvement less comfortable on the road and finally keep a complete win.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Pastoria ran for forty-two yards against Lavender, leaving its passing game to carry most of the scoring work. I expect Mahogany to make that imbalance harder to sustain, with the home offense taking enough possession to control a close result.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Frost's season has contained more competitive football than its three wins suggest. I expect the bye to help turn that into a proper result, even against a Pastoria team whose passing revival deserves to be taken seriously.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Pastoria scored seventeen and would now like a parade for completing the assignment. Mahogany has a stronger season-long scoring balance. I expect the Frost to make the Waves earn longer drives, then finish enough of their own to settle it.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mahogany's stronger scoring balance and home advantage outweigh Pastoria's single improved passing result for me. I expect the Frost to keep the Waves' rushing limited, forcing enough difficult passing possessions to preserve a one-score advantage.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Blackthorn is 8–1, and Hatterene just completed seventeen of twenty-one. Sunyshore has had a week to rest and remain irritating. I expect the Dragons' passing efficiency to make the visitors pay for the few possessions their running game cannot protect.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Hearthome held Blackthorn to forty-nine rushing yards and still nearly won the passing exchange. I expect Sunyshore's more balanced recent offense to keep Hatterene waiting, then create enough scoring chances to justify the difficult road pick.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Dragons escaped by two while the Starseekers had time to prepare. I think Sunyshore's useful rushing response at Lavender can travel, giving the visitors the patient possessions needed to win without pretending Hatterene will suddenly become careless.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Hatterene has supplied another efficient win, and Clair's team is 8–1. Sunyshore's bye does not come with points attached. I expect Blackthorn's passing to make the Starseekers chase the game, then force the road offense into the less comfortable choices.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Sunyshore's latest balance gives it a narrow route to controlling possession against a Blackthorn team that just struggled to run. I expect enough of that rushing support to survive the trip and create one more decisive scoring opportunity.
